## Eleven packages, three ways to compose them

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  DJ["Distributions.jl"]
  EXT["Censored<br>Convolved<br>Modified<br>Reparameterised"]
  CMP["Composed<br>Distributions.jl"]
  LOW["Lowered<br>Distributions.jl"]
  A["A<br>Distributions<br>Inference.jl"]
  B["B<br>ComposableTuring<br>IDModels.jl"]
  C["C<br>SciML<br>solvers"]
  SCR["Scoring<br>Rules.jl"]
  NXT["Generation<br>Time.jl<br>Reproduction<br>Number.jl"]

  DJ --> EXT --> CMP
  DJ --> LOW --> C
  CMP --> A --> SCR
  CMP --> B --> SCR
  C --> SCR
  NXT -.-> CMP
  NXT -.-> B

  classDef empty stroke-dasharray:6 4,color:#777,stroke:#777
  class NXT empty
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
- **A.** Composed distributions plus a fitting layer,
  `DistributionsInference.jl`. `rand` simulates a case, `logpdf` scores
  one
- **B.** Turing submodels. Joint inference and the whole toolchain, and
  one PPL's decisions with it
- **C.** SciML. A delay becomes a generator, with solvers and
  sensitivities. Inference supplied separately
- We run all three and keep them interoperable because I cannot tell
  you which is right

::: {.callout-note}
Two more talks from me take one route each. Route A at 14:45, delay
distributions. Route B at 16:45, composable models.
:::
:::
::::

::: {.attribution}
22 repositories, 19 of them public. 11 hold a Julia package, 10 of those
are registered in General. `ScoringRules.jl` is not, and the two dashed
packages are empty repositories. The other two hold the rest rigid.
`EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` is on the next slide,
`EpiAwareADTools.jl` in the section after it. Counted on 2026-08-10.
:::

## What holds it together, and what does not

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="46%"}
```julia
const BANNED_README_WORDS = [
    "comprehensive", "cornerstone",
    "facilitate", "foster",
    "framework", "harness",
    "landscape", "leverage",
    "novel", "pivotal",
    "practitioner", "robust",
    "streamline", "synergy",
    # ... 20 in total
]
```

::: {.callout-note}
A guideline gets ignored. A failing test does not.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="54%"}
- Nine quality checks run in every package. `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl`
  writes up to 69 files into one, most force-managed, so a package
  cannot drift. Ten of the eleven are on it
- The bill is 8,600 lines of Julia to hold ten packages rigid, and a
  contributor cannot change one repository's tooling on their own
- The people half is not started. In R the community came with the
  packages. The epinowcast forum has 144 members and 1,273 posts, and we
  have run 34 seminars since May 2023, roughly monthly
- On the Julia side there is no seminar, no category on that forum, and
  the team page lists one maintainer. Nothing names a first task, and no
  open issue in the org is labelled a good first issue

::: {.attribution}
[community.epinowcast.org](https://community.epinowcast.org) and
[epinowcast.org/seminars](https://www.epinowcast.org/seminars.html),
read 2026-08-10 · every package carries the label, none of the open
issues use it, searched 2026-08-10.
:::
:::
::::

## What ships next

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
**September 2026. Nothing red.**
`ComposedDistributions.jl` green on all six backends,
`ScoringRules.jl` registered, and the documentation site level with
`main` rather than trailing it.

**December 2026. The dynamics components.**
`GenerationTime.jl` and `ReproductionNumber.jl`, the two empty
repositories, are the disease dynamics pieces the abstract promised.

**March 2027. A written way in.**
A governance document saying how a package joins and who decides, and a
contributing guide that names a first task.
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.callout-important}
Three dates. Come and find me at JuliaCon 2027 if none of them happened.
:::

- Order matters. Fix what is red before adding packages, and write the
  governance down before asking anyone else to depend on this
- `SpeedyWeather.jl` is the size and shape we are aiming at. One domain,
  a handful of packages, and users who are modellers rather than
  developers
- The abstract for this talk says we have one package and an R
  prototype, `EpiAwareR`. It is ten packages out of date
:::
::::
